question: Will Russia's State Duma adopt in first reading, before 13 November 2026, a bill moving the launch of pre-bankruptcy rehabilitation to 1 January 2027?

calls.reasoning: Status quo as of 30 Oct: both bills awaiting first reading, no date set. Bill 5261-9 (co-sponsored by the responsible committee's chair Gavrilov) was reportedly backed by the committee and put into the Duma Council's November programme, with feedback closing 29 Oct (smart-lab, 23 Oct; secondary source, unverified in SOZD). The November programme likely spans ~3 plenary weeks (10-12, 17-19, 24-26 Nov) and only the first falls inside the window; the budget's second reading (~19 Nov) is crowding the agenda. Pressure from Samolet, the Economy Ministry and Delovaya Rossiya argues for speed, but no 10-12 Nov agenda listing was found. No human market found on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers.

calls.reasoning: Both bills (1308850-8, 5261-9) were awaiting first reading with no date set as of 30 Oct 2026; no newer reporting of a committee recommendation or agenda slot was found. Support: MinEk backs the 1 Jan 2027 date, the committee chair Gavrilov co-wrote 5261-9, Samolet distress adds urgency, and a 1 Jan 2027 start needs passage by late December. Roughly P(passes in 2026)~0.62 x P(first reading in the 10-12 Nov week | passes)~0.35 gives ~0.22. No human prediction market found.

calls.reconciliation: Main factual dispute: was 5261-9 really backed by the committee and put in the Duma Council's November programme? Run 1 relied on this; Runs 2-3 treated it as unverified. I opened the smart-lab post (23 Oct 2026), and it states verbatim that the property committee supported it, the Council put it in the November programme, and comments closed 29 Oct. Still secondary, not checked in SOZD. Second check: a search for a 10-12 Nov agenda or any first-reading date for the bill found nothing, only confirmation that 10/11 Nov are plenary days (wine bills). The mail.ru article of 30 Oct gives no procedural timing. One search summary claiming the bill was 'submitted 5 Nov 2026' is a summariser artefact and was ignored. Remaining judgment: what share of a November-programme first reading lands in the first week. Comments closed 29 Oct, the 1 Jan deadline is urgent and the bill's author chairs the committee, which pushes toward the earliest slot. Budget crowding and no announced date push against. I land at 0.34, close to Run 1 because the disputed premise is supported, and below 0.5 because no agenda placement is confirmed. No human prediction market found.
